text:
maya: Heads up — noticed missing per-sample traces for quantized-v2 during batch evals after we flipped on multipart + gzip in the runner. run-2026-03-18-09. Anybody seen this before?

samir: can you paste the artifact-uploader logs?

maya: log snippet: 
```
ERROR s3-uploader: upload failed for part 7: IncompleteBody: You provided a Content-Length header for 1048576 bytes, but the body had fewer bytes.
uploadId: xyz-123
parts_total: 42
```
seems intermittent across many runs, but only when `gzip: true` and `multipart: true`. single-part uploads fine.

alexa: gzip stream + multipart is dangerous — gzip produces a stream where chunk boundaries matter. if we're chunking the stream mid-compression, parts can be invalid. we usually either: 1) compress whole file then multipart, or 2) compress per-record.

jordan: +1. quick mitigation: set `part_size` >= final gzip file size so it becomes single part. annoying but works as a short-term stopgap.

infra-bot: s3-uploader v1.4.2 reported 42 failed part(s) across 6 uploads in the last 2h.

samir: either buffer gz to disk and multipart that, or gzip each sample before concatenation (but that bloats headers). i prefer buffering gz to temp file: then MD5s computed per-part are stable.

maya: implementation detail idea: modify runner uploader to do `if gzip && multipart: write_gzip_to_tempfile(); multipart_upload(tempfile)` — less memory pressure than buffering whole batch in RAM? we'll still need disk.

alexa: agree. also add per-part `x-amz-meta-chunk-sha256` so we can validate parts during backfill/diagnostics.

samir: open a quick PR? i can review. also need a CI test that simulates splitting a gzip stream into random part sizes and reassembles on recv side.

maya: created draft PR #2345 with patch and test harness: `runner/tests/test_multipart_gzip_roundtrip.py` — the test uses random part sizes and asserts final file matches original uncompressed bytes.

ci-bot: PR #2345: unit tests total 1245, new tests 6, status: queued -> running -> PASS 

alexa: nice. for retention/indexing: we lost some per-sample metadata links when parts dropped. let's add `artifact_manifest.jsonl` at root of artifact with per-sample offsets + checksums so downstream trace DB can recover. example manifest entry: `{"sample_idx": 12, "offset": 12345, "length": 987, "sha256": "..."}`

jordan: that manifest approach is good. also update the uploader to emit `ETag` + `part_checksums` in the object's metadata so we can cross-check during rehydration.

maya: planned steps: 1) merge PR #2345 to staging, 2) run canary on `quantized/v2-7b-int8` evals, 3) enable manifest + per-part metadata, 4) schedule backfill job to detect missing samples and reupload if possible.

samir: i'll review the PR today. also create a lightweight CI integration test that runs on a real S3 (minio) to catch edgecases.

maya: reassigning to @samir for review, and tagging @alexa for manifest schema review. i'll post run results here after staging canary. :rocket:

infra-bot: staged upload succeeded: run-2026-03-18-09-canary, parts: 5, gzip: true, manifest present.

maya: staging canary looks good so far — no missing traces in 10/10 runs. rolling to prod tomorrow morning.

ci-bot: nightly integration job (minio) added for multipart+gzip roundtrip. next scheduled run: 2026-03-19T04:00:00Z.

alexa: one follow-up: update eval dashboard to surface `manifest_missing_count` and `part_mismatch_count` for artifact health. small alert if >0 for 5 mins.

maya: will add dashboard card + alert. tagging incident runbook update too.

samir: comment left on PR re: tempfile cleanup on OOM paths. otherwise LGTM.

maya: thanks all — will post final prod rollout note in #eng-ml once done.
